items.stem: Which of the following is a feature of marketing goods rather than services?
options: Goods cannot be separated from the provider
Goods can be stored as inventory
Goods are perishable at the point of delivery
items.answer: Goods can be stored as inventory
items.markingKey: C. Services are intangible and perishable.

items.stem: Briefly explain why market orientation can reduce the risk of product failure.
items.answer: Products are designed around researched customer needs, so demand is more likely to exist at launch; feedback can be used to adapt products before large sums are invested.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Products are designed around researched customer needs, so demand is more likely to exist at launch; feedback can be used to adapt products before large sums are invested. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between product orientation and market orientation.
items.answer: A market-oriented firm starts from customer research and designs products to satisfy needs; a product-oriented firm starts from what it can make well and then looks for buyers.
items.markingKey: A market-oriented firm starts from customer research and designs products to satisfy needs; a product-oriented firm starts from what it can make well and then looks for buyers. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Outline one way in which Netflix's viewing data shows market orientation.
items.answer: Netflix uses viewing data from over 270 million subscribers to decide which series to commission and how to recommend them. Customer data drives product decisions, reducing the risk of commissioning unpopular content
items.markingKey: Context (Netflix uses viewing data from over 270 million subscribers to decide which series to commission and how to recommend them.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Customer data drives product decisions, reducing the risk of commissioning unpopular content – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to market orientation.

items.stem: A student claims: "Marketing is the same as advertising." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Advertising is only one part of promotion; marketing includes research, product development, pricing, distribution and customer service.
items.markingKey: Advertising is only one part of promotion; marketing includes research, product development, pricing, distribution and customer service. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Market orientation is always better than product orientation."
items.answer: Market orientation suits most firms, but a balance is best: radical innovators may need a product-led approach backed by later market testing.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: reduces risk of failure; products meet customer needs; easier to adapt to change. Arguments against: customers may not imagine radical innovations; research is costly and slow; product-led innovators such as Dyson succeed; copying customer wishes may reduce creativity. Supported judgement: Market orientation suits most firms, but a balance is best: radical innovators may need a product-led approach backed by later market testing.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "An approach in which a business focuses on making a product it is good at, then tries to find customers to buy it"?
items.answer: product orientation
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of product orientation.

items.stem: A hotel chain plans a large advertising campaign. Explain how the campaign affects the human resources and operations functions.
items.answer: HR may need to recruit and train extra staff for higher demand; operations must ensure rooms, food and services can handle more guests at the promised quality, or the campaign will damage the brand.
items.markingKey: HR may need to recruit and train extra staff for higher demand; operations must ensure rooms, food and services can handle more guests at the promised quality, or the campaign will damage the brand.

items.answer: It avoids direct competition with large mass-market firms, allows premium prices for specialised products and builds customer loyalty with a small budget.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "niche market"?

A feature that makes a product different from and preferred to competitors' products

items.answer: A small, well-defined segment of a market with specific needs

items.stem: Explain why market share is a useful measure of a firm's performance.
items.answer: It shows performance relative to competitors rather than in isolation; a rising share means the firm is winning customers, which can bring economies of scale and bargaining power.

items.stem: Explain the difference between mass marketing and niche marketing.
items.answer: Niche marketing targets a small segment with specialised products, often at premium prices; mass marketing sells a largely standard product to the whole market at high volume.
items.markingKey: Niche marketing targets a small segment with specialised products, often at premium prices; mass marketing sells a largely standard product to the whole market at high volume. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between a USP and product differentiation.
items.answer: A USP is one specific feature that makes a product unique; product differentiation is the broader process of making a product different from rivals in any way.
items.markingKey: A USP is one specific feature that makes a product unique; product differentiation is the broader process of making a product different from rivals in any way. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why some firms in high-technology markets remain product oriented.
items.answer: Customers may not know they want a radical new technology until it exists, so firms rely on research and development to create products and then persuade customers to buy them.

items.stem: Explain the difference between market growth and market share.
items.answer: Market growth measures how fast the whole market is expanding; market share measures one firm's position within it.
